title: Query one partition
summary: Query selects one partition key and can return its related items.
introduction: Query selects one partition key and can return its related items. Your task: Explain why this query does not read every reader partition.

Explain the example for query one partition

blocks.text: Query selects one partition key and can return its related items. It is different from scanning the entire table.

Use DynamoDB Local and the AWS CLI or SDK in a separate practice project. Point every command at http://localhost:8000. Low-level JSON examples show request bodies; provide them to the matching CLI command or SDK method.
Read the code step by step

items: `KeyConditionExpression` uses the table or index keys to select a partition and, optionally, a sort-key range.
`ConditionExpression` checks the current item as part of the write, so a failed condition prevents the change.
`ExpressionAttributeNames` maps placeholders such as #reader to actual field names in the request expression.

blocks.text: The local query returns items in Mia's partition, ordered by their sort keys.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A key condition must fit the table or index key. An arbitrary non-key field needs a different design or a filter after reading.
